- `/home/salem/payment-gateway/admin-back/test/admin-search-surface.test.ts` or extend `admin-surface.test.ts`
  - LAN guard, session header, edge query validation, forwarding path, core error relay, rate-limit behavior.
- `/home/salem/payment-gateway/tests/e2e/admin/global-search.spec.ts`
  - Ctrl+K opens palette, typing calls `/api/v1/admin/search`, groups render, unauthorized group is absent, selecting a result routes to the correct detail page.
  - Also add a11y and Arabic/RTL checks.

---

## 7. Existing global search / command palette / cross-entity code

### There is no server-side global search today

The only “global search” in `admin-front` is a **local guide content palette**:

- `/home/salem/payment-gateway/admin-front/src/layouts/default.tsx:135-139`
  ```ts
  if ((event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === "k") {
    event.preventDefault();
    guideSearchOpen.value = true;
  }
  ```
- `/home/salem/payment-gateway/admin-front/src/layouts/default.tsx:353-357` — sidebar pill says `Search guide, rails, cases…`, but it opens the guide modal.
- `/home/salem/payment-gateway/admin-front/src/layouts/default.tsx:452-459` — selection always routes to `AdminGuide`, not to entity detail pages.
- `/home/salem/payment-gateway/admin-front/src/components/guide/GlobalGuideSearchModal.tsx:31-45, 70-84` — `searchGuide(query)` local only; no HTTP.
- `/home/salem/payment-gateway/admin-front/src/content/guide/search.ts:190-239` — in-memory index, substring scoring, limit 60 from the modal.
- Design confirms this scope: `/home/salem/payment-gateway/design/guide_system_design_and_content (2).md:83-85` lists global command palette in scope but explicitly says **server-side search is out of scope**.

### Closest existing cross-entity backend code

- `/home/salem/payment-gateway/core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:923-1019` — `GET /options/:kind`.
  - After `requireAuthentication`, but **no per-resource authority check**.
  - Kinds: `merchants`, `rails`, `gateways`, `users`, `applications`, `wallets`, `credential-sets`, `gl-accounts`.
  - Search fields: merchant `tradeName`/`legalName`; rail `code`/`nameEn`/`nameAr`; gateway `code`/`name`; user `email`/`phone`; application `name`; wallet `currency`; credential set `externalMerchantId`; GL accounts filter by `ownerId` only.
  - `limit` default 50, max 100 (`OPTION_LIMIT` at line 921).
  - Response `{ items: [{ value, title, subtitle? }], total: items.length }`; `total` is the returned count, not DB count.
  - Frontend consumer: `/home/salem/payment-gateway/admin-front/src/components/Table/referenceOptions.ts:8-19`, with an unbounded in-memory cache keyed `kind:search`.
- `/home/salem/payment-gateway/core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:730-891` — `GET /stats/overview` aggregates merchants, attempts, approvals, join requests, AML, operator cases, route health, recon, but has no search parameter.
- `/home/salem/payment-gateway/core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:676-728` — recent activity is an audit-log cross-entity feed, not searchable.
- `DataTable` server search is per-table only: `/home/salem/payment-gateway/admin-front/src/components/Table/DataTable.tsx:65-104`, sending `search`, `sortKey`, `sortDirection`, filters and `page=1,pageSize=200`. It is not cross-entity.

### Recommended search contract for the new endpoint

Because existing list endpoints return inconsistent keys and sensitive fields, do **not** simply fan out an internal HTTP call to all list endpoints. Build one core aggregator with explicit per-type specs and serializers.

Suggested response shape:

```ts
{
  query: string,
  groups: Array<{
    type: "merchant" | "attempt" | "dispute" | ...,
    label: string,
    items: Array<{
      id: string,
      title: string,
      subtitle?: string,
      reference?: string,
      status?: string,
      merchantId?: string,
      deepLink: { name: string, params?: Record<string, string> },
    }>,
    truncated: boolean,
  }>,
  total: number,
  partial: boolean,
}
```

Suggested query parameters:

- `search` (consistent with all list endpoints; optionally alias `q`)
- `types` comma-separated allow-list
- `limit` per group, max 20-50
- optional `cursor` only if the implementation becomes paged; existing lists use page/pageSize, but a command palette should prefer a bounded per-type `take`

Suggested authority matrix for groups:

- Merchants, join requests, KYB: `merchant:read` / `kyb:read` / `compliance:read`, with `SUPPORT` field restrictions.
- Users: `user:read` or `security:read`.
- Approvals: `approval:read`.
- AML cases/screenings: confidential only; omit group and counts entirely otherwise.
- Operator cases/gateway inquiries: `case:read` or `operator:read`.
- Disputes: `dispute:read`; adjustments: `finance:read`; cashouts: `cashout:read`.
- Gateways/rails/routes: `gateway:read`; credential sets: `credential:read` or `gateway:read`.
- Reconciliation runs: `reconciliation:read`.
- Audit logs: `security:read`; return action/entity IDs only, not `beforeJson`/`afterJson`.
- Payment attempts: currently no top-level list; decide explicitly whether to expose an `attempt` group and hydrate merchant/rail/status with the same `SUPPORT` redaction as `/merchants/:id/transactions` (`admin.ts:4720-4830`). A payment reference is likely the highest-value search key for support, so this should probably be included.

Important implementation constraints:

- Enforce all authority and redaction in **core**, because the edge authority guard is coarse and decodes the JWT without signature verification.
- Do not leak hidden-group existence through `total`, group counts, or “no results” wording. Compute totals after the authority gate.
- Reuse the existing `ApiError` and `listResponse`-style conventions, not a new response dialect.
- Add explicit search length and wildcard normalization; the existing core helper accepts arbitrary strings and relies on Prisma parameterization.
- Consider a dedicated per-identity rate limit; the existing admin limiter is globally bucketed by socket IP and the core internal channel has none.
- Avoid logging raw search text in `admin-back` query URLs, or explicitly redact it, because `requestLogger` logs `originalUrl`.

<task id="ses_e628f798dffeLGAITJWywhnoxo" state="completed">
<task_result>
# Admin search research: admin-back (BFF) and core-back

No existing server-side global/deep search endpoint was found. Search is currently per-resource via the shared list contract, plus a lightweight `/options/:kind` autocomplete route. There is no BFF `/search` router and no core `/internal/admin/search` route.

---

## 1. Protected route organization and forwarding

### Boot and mounting chain

- `admin-back/index.ts:9-23` creates the app, installs request logging, health, JSON/urlencoded parsing, then mounts the API:
  - `app.use("/api/v1/admin", enforceLanAccess, apiRouter)` at `admin-back/index.ts:20`.
  - `notFoundHandler` and `apiErrorHandler` follow at lines 21-22.
- `admin-back/api/index.ts:5-10` mounts:
  - public auth at `router.use("/auth", adminAuthRouter)` (line 7)
  - everything else through `router.use("/", protectedRouter)` (line 8)
- `admin-back/api/protected/index.ts:24-63`:
  - creates one `express.Router`;
  - installs `adminLimiter` at line 39 and `requireSession` at line 40;
  - mounts one router per domain at lines 42-59: `/academy`, `/users`, `/join-requests`, `/merchants`, `/approvals`, `/aml`, `/gateways`, `/gateway-versions`, `/credential-sets`, `/rails`, `/routes`, `/assets`, `/reconciliation`, `/settings`, `/options`, `/stats`, `/audit-logs`, `/kyb-documents`;
  - mounts `operationsRouter` and `financeRouter` at `/` last (lines 60-61). A cross-cutting `/search` router should be added before these root mounts.

### Route module pattern

Each domain file owns an `express.Router` and declares routes inline. Example, `admin-back/api/protected/stats.ts:7-78`:

```ts
const overviewQuerySchema = z
  .object({ period: z.enum(["24h", "7d", "30d", "90d"]).optional() })
  .passthrough();

router.get("/overview", coreForward({
  method: "GET",
  path: () => "/internal/admin/stats/overview",
  querySchema: overviewQuerySchema,
}));
```

`admin-back/api/protected/merchants.ts:136-198` shows the list/detail pattern: list uses `zPaginationQuery`; detail paths validate `paramsSchema` and encode path params with `encodeURIComponent`.

### `coreForward` pipeline

`admin-back/api/forward.ts:15-39` defines options:

- `method`, `path(context)`, optional `schema`, `paramsSchema`, `querySchema`, `status`;
- `bodyFrom(req, body)` for public→core write translation;
- `splitBodyFrom` for fan-out writes;
- `headers`, `relayStatus`.

Execution is at `admin-back/api/forward.ts:52-92`:

1. Validate `req.params` with `paramsSchema` and `req.query` with `querySchema` (lines 55-61).
2. For GET/HEAD, body is undefined (lines 62-63).
3. For writes, validate public body with `schema` first (lines 64-65).
4. Call `callCoreResponse` with method/path/body/query and identity headers (lines 66-77).
5. Apply `bodyFrom` before sending (line 89).
6. Respond with declared status, or core’s status when `relayStatus: true` (line 91).

Important query detail: `scalarQuery` at `admin-back/api/forward.ts:41-50` forwards only string/number/boolean values. Array query parameters are dropped. Multi-value filters must therefore be comma-separated strings, e.g. `types=merchants,gateways`, matching core’s CSV parsing.

There is no timeout option in `ForwardOptions`. The only per-call timeout override today is the upload path, `admin-back/api/upload.ts:61-80`, which passes `timeoutMs: env.RECONCILIATION_TIMEOUT_MS`.

### Contract pattern

`admin-back/api/contract.ts:4-19` is the translation layer only for writes:

- core’s schemas are `.strict()`;
- mappers emit only accepted keys and required keys;
- mappers are pure `(public body) => core body`.

Reads/lists do not use `contract.ts`; their response is returned verbatim. A GET search endpoint should normally need no contract mapper.

### Core route registration

- `core-back/index.ts:61-69` builds the Express app.
- `core-back/index.ts:111-112` mounts `/internal` and `/api`.
- `core-back/api/index.ts:13-16` binds each internal namespace to a client certificate CN:
  - `/internal/admin` → `requireEdgeIdentity("admin-back")`
  - `/internal/merchant` → `merchant-back`
  - `/internal/checkout` → `checkout-back`
- `core-back/api/internal/index.ts:1-12` only re-exports the three routers.
- `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts` is one large router:
  - `/health` at line 169;
  - unauthenticated `/auth/login`, `/auth/mfa`, `/auth/me` at lines 561, 628, 665;
  - `router.use(requireAuthentication)` at line 674;
  - all protected admin routes follow;
  - exported as `adminInternalRouter` at line 15986.

A new core search route must be registered after line 674, otherwise it bypasses authentication.

---

## 2. Authority enforcement and context propagation

### BFF enforcement

**LAN guard**

- `admin-back/index.ts:20` applies `enforceLanAccess` to every `/api/v1/admin/*` request.
- `admin-back/api/middleware/lanGuard.ts:16-32`:
  - trusts forwarded headers only from loopback or `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`;
  - resolves client IP through `resolveClientIp`;
  - rejects outside `ADMIN_LAN_CIDRS` with `403 ADMIN_LAN_ONLY`.

**Protected router guards**

- `admin-back/api/protected/index.ts:39` installs the rate limiter.
- `admin-back/api/protected/index.ts:40` installs `requireSession`.
- `admin-back/api/middleware/authorityGuard.ts:114-119`: `requireSession` only checks that an `Authorization` header exists. It does not validate the token.
- BFF route-level authority is only used for AML:
  - `admin-back/api/protected/aml.ts:21` defines
    `requireAuthorities("COMPLIANCE", "MLRO", "aml:read", "aml:write")`;
  - mounted for the whole AML router at `admin-back/api/protected/aml.ts:134`.
  - All other domain routers rely on core authentication/authorization.

**BFF authority-hint decoding**

`admin-back/api/middleware/authorityGuard.ts:45-112`:

- splits a Bearer JWT, decodes the payload segment without verifying the signature;
- accepts only:
  - `typ` absent or `"session"`;
  - `iss` absent or `"payment-gateway-core"`;
  - `aud` absent or containing `"payment-gateway-edge"`;
- reads roles from `role` / `roles`;
- reads authorities from `authorities` and legacy `authorities_map`.

`requireAuthorities` at lines 123-163:

- normalizes to upper case;
- filters required authorities against `ADMIN_AUTHORITY_HINTS`;
- if the configured list contains none of the requested authorities, it calls `next()` and effectively disables the check (lines 130-137);
- otherwise any-of matching against roles/authorities and `ROLE_AUTHORITY_ALIASES` (COMPLIANCE/MLRO → `AML:READ`, `AML:WRITE`) at lines 148-153.

Planning consequence: if a new BFF search route declares authorities not present in `ADMIN_AUTHORITY_HINTS`, the edge guard silently passes. Add the authority names to `admin-back/lib/env/index.ts:32-36` or do not add a BFF guard.

### Core enforcement

**mTLS identity**

- TLS server requires client certs at `core-back/index.ts:153-160`.
- `core-back/api/middleware/mtlsGuard.ts:19-49` verifies:
  - `socket.authorized`;
  - peer certificate CN exists;
  - CN equals expected service name.
- A new route under `/internal/admin` automatically inherits this guard.

**Session authentication**

- `core-back/api/middleware/authDoubleCheck.ts:123-152` verifies the session token, loads the user from DB, requires `status === "ACTIVE"`, parses `authoritiesMap`, and rejects empty authorities.
- `core-back/lib/auth/index.ts:101-119` verifies HS256 signature, issuer `payment-gateway-core`, audience `payment-gateway-edge`.
- `core-back/lib/auth/index.ts:66-76` mints a 12-hour session token.
- `core-back/api/middleware/authDoubleCheck.ts:165-199`:
  - `requireAuthentication` sets `request.principal`;
  - `requireAuthorities(request, required)` is ANY-of and supports `"*"`.

**Per-route authority declarations**

Core declares authority inside each handler, not via route middleware. Examples:

- users list: `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:1023-1030` — `requireAuthorities(request, ["user:read", "security:read"])`.
- merchants list: `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:4196-4199` — `requireAuthorities(request, ["merchant:read"])`, then `principalOf` and `merchantOperationalFlags`.
- audit logs: `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:15488-15490` — `requireAuthorities(request, ["security:read"])`.

Special confidential checks:

- `assertConfidential` at `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:193-206` for AML confidentiality, using roles or `aml:read`/`aml:write`.
- `assertReportingAuthority` at lines 220-234 for regulatory reporting.
- merchant visibility flags at `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:3840-3847`; underlying helpers at `core-back/lib/merchantOps.ts:121-138`:
  - `hasSensitiveMerchantAccess`
  - `hasMerchantAmlAccess`
  - `hasMerchantFinancialAccess`
  - `SUPPORT` is explicitly denied sensitive/AML/financial views.

For a global search, core must filter result types by the authenticated principal. A single top-level `requireAuthorities` ANY-of check would let a user with one domain authority see everything returned by the endpoint.

### Headers and user context

BFF builds core headers at `admin-back/lib/mtlsClient/index.ts:205-220`:

- `x-request-id`
- `x-real-client-ip`
- `x-client-user-agent`
- `x-edge-service: admin-back`
- `accept: application/json`
- `authorization` unchanged
- `content-type` when a body exists

BFF resolves client IP at `admin-back/lib/net/index.ts:137-145`:

- `X-Real-IP` is preferred when the immediate peer is trusted;
- `X-Real-Client-IP` is only a fallback;
- otherwise the socket address is used.

Core uses:

- `x-real-client-ip` for API-token IP allowlisting in `core-back/api/middleware/authDoubleCheck.ts:79-85`;
- `x-request-id` in `core-back/index.ts:27-40`, which validates it and echoes it in the response;
- user/principal context from the bearer token, not from custom user headers.

---

## 3. Existing list/search proxy behavior

### Representative list routes

BFF:

- merchants list: `admin-back/api/protected/merchants.ts:136-143`
- users list: `admin-back/api/protected/users.ts:83-90`
- audit logs list: `admin-back/api/protected/auditLogs.ts:7-14`

Pattern:

```ts
router.get("/", coreForward({
  method: "GET",
  path: () => "/internal/admin/<resource>",
  querySchema: zPaginationQuery,
}));
```

Core then uses `buildListQuery` and `listResponse`.

### Query validation and parameter handling

BFF list schema: `admin-back/lib/zReady/index.ts:63-77`.

- `zListQuery` validates:
  - `search` max 200;
  - `page` 1..10000;
  - `pageSize` 1..200;
  - `sortKey`, `sortDirection`;
  - `from`, `to`, `dateFrom`, `dateTo`.
- `.passthrough()` allows domain-specific filters.
- `zPaginationQuery` is an alias of `zListQuery`.

Forwarding behavior:

- `querySchema` output is passed through `scalarQuery` at `admin-back/api/forward.ts:41-50`.
- Arrays are dropped; use CSV strings.
- `admin-back/lib/mtlsClient/index.ts:157-176` serializes scalars with `URLSearchParams`.

Core parsing/building:

- `core-back/lib/listQuery.ts:49-70` parses strings, trims, clamps `pageSize` to 1..200, defaults to 50.
- `core-back/lib/listQuery.ts:139-221`:
  - `search` becomes OR-ed `contains` over declared dot paths;
  - `contains` filters OR paths for one key and AND different keys;
  - `in` accepts comma-separated values;
  - dates are inclusive (`from` start-of-day, `to` end-of-day);
  - ranges use `Prisma.Decimal` or `Number`;
  - only whitelisted `sortable` keys are honored, then `{ id: "desc" }`;
  - pagination uses `skip`/`take`.

Examples of search field declarations:

- users: `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:1025-1030` (`email`, `phone`).
- merchants: `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:4200-4225` (`legalName`, `tradeName`, contact fields, sensitive fields when authorized).
- audit logs: `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:15490-15503` (`action`, `entityType`, `entityId`, `actor.email`).
- options autocomplete: `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:923-1019`, `search` + `limit` across specific kinds; response `{ items, total }` at line 1019, capped by `OPTION_LIMIT = 100` at line 921.

### Response shape

Core returns the body directly; BFF does not wrap or rename it. `core-back/api/forward.ts:90-91` simply sends `response.body`.

Core’s `listResponse` at `core-back/lib/listQuery.ts:223-228`:

```ts
{ [key]: rows, total, page, pageSize }
```

Examples:

- `GET /api/v1/admin/merchants` → `{ merchants, total, page, pageSize }` (`core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:4274-4279`).
- `GET /api/v1/admin/users` → `{ users, total, page, pageSize }` (`core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:1042-1056`).
- `GET /api/v1/admin/audit-logs` → `{ auditLogs, total, page, pageSize }` (`core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:15514-15526`).

There is no global `data` envelope and no `totalPages`. A global search should either follow `listResponse("results", ...)` or define a deliberate grouped shape; consistency favors a single result array with a `type` discriminator.

### Timeout and error handling

- BFF default core timeout: `CORE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 60,000 ms (`admin-back/lib/env/index.ts:22`), applied at `admin-back/lib/mtlsClient/index.ts:243`.
- Upload uses `RECONCILIATION_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 120,000 ms (`admin-back/lib/env/index.ts:44`; `admin-back/api/upload.ts:79`).
- Transport errors are mapped at `admin-back/lib/mtlsClient/index.ts:117-134`:
  - timeout → `504 CORE_TIMEOUT`
  - connection refused/reset/host unreachable → `502 CORE_UNREACHABLE`
  - DNS → `502 CORE_DNS_FAILURE`
  - TLS → `502 CORE_TLS_ERROR`
- Core HTTP errors preserve core’s envelope via `mapCoreHttpError` at `admin-back/lib/mtlsClient/index.ts:95-108`: `{ code, message, details?, reference? }`.
- BFF error handler serializes `ApiError` at `admin-back/lib/error/index.ts:65-84`.
- Core error envelope is built at `core-back/lib/error/index.ts:62-100`; core adds the request id as `reference`.
- Core app error handler is at `core-back/index.ts:114-138`.

Special non-`coreForward` paths:

- binary KYB content uses `callCoreRaw` and manually copies headers/status: `admin-back/api/protected/kybReview.ts:136-154`;
- upload uses `callCore` with a longer timeout: `admin-back/api/upload.ts:41-81`;
- fan-out bulk writes use `callCoreResponse` loops: `admin-back/api/protected/users.ts:125-149`, `admin-back/api/protected/approvals.ts:83-120`, `admin-back/api/protected/joinRequests.ts` around lines 172-200.

If search needs a custom timeout, `coreForward` must be extended or the route must call `callCoreResponse` directly.

---

## 4. Is one BFF `/v1/admin/search` endpoint consistent?

Structurally yes, if it is a thin proxy to a new core endpoint. It is not consistent as a BFF-only aggregate that calls multiple core list endpoints.

Reasons:

- BFF has no database access (`admin-back/README.md:5-9`).
- Every existing protected route is a one-to-one forward to `/internal/admin/...`.
- BFF fan-out exists only for bulk writes, not cross-domain reads.
- Different list endpoints require different core authorities and return different collection keys and serialized fields.
- A BFF-only fan-out would need to swallow per-endpoint 403s, merge pagination, dedupe results, and filter sensitive fields itself, duplicating core policy.
- The clean design is one core endpoint that authenticates the principal, applies per-type visibility, queries with `buildListQuery`, and returns one consistent result shape.

Actual path note: the BFF is mounted at `/api/v1/admin` (`admin-back/index.ts:20`), so the endpoint would be `/api/v1/admin/search`, not `/v1/admin/search` unless the mount changes.

### Recommended shape

BFF route:

```ts
router.get("/", coreForward({
  method: "GET",
  path: () => "/internal/admin/search",
  querySchema: zPaginationQuery, // or a dedicated zSearchQuery
}));
```

Core route, registered after `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:674`, should:

- call `principalOf(request)` / `requireAuthentication` context;
- optionally require at least one relevant authority, but primarily filter by type;
- use `buildListQuery` per searched model;
- return `listResponse("results", rows, total, built)` or a grouped result object;
- apply AML confidentiality (`assertConfidential`, lines 193-206) and merchant flags (`merchantOperationalFlags`, lines 3840-3847) to result fields;
- avoid returning raw sensitive fields for `SUPPORT` or users without the relevant authority.

### Files that would need changes

Required:

1. `admin-back/api/protected/search.ts` — new router, with a search query schema and `coreForward` GET to `/internal/admin/search`.
2. `admin-back/api/protected/index.ts` — import and mount:
   ```ts
   import { searchRouter } from "./search";
   router.use("/search", searchRouter);
   ```
   Place it before the root-mounted `operationsRouter`/`financeRouter` at lines 60-61.
3. `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts` — add the core search handler after line 674, or add a new helper module such as `core-back/api/internal/search.ts` and import/mount it inside `admin.ts`. The existing `adminInternalRouter` export at line 15986 stays the same.
4. Tests:
   - `admin-back/test/admin-surface.test.ts:1129-1332` — add the BFF route to the route-surface list and assert it forwards to `/internal/admin/search`.
   - `core-back/test/internal-routes.test.ts:46-67` — add authentication/authority/validation tests for the core route.
   - `core-back/test/list-query.test.ts` or a new search test — cover search, type filters, pagination, sorting, date ranges, and per-authority filtering.

Likely/optional:

5. `admin-back/lib/zReady/index.ts:63-77` — reuse `zListQuery`, or add a dedicated search query schema if fields like `types`/`scope` need stricter validation.
6. `admin-back/README.md:13-33` — document the new route and any new env vars.
7. `admin-back/test/helpers/core-schema.ts` and `admin-back/test/core-contract.test.ts:909-940` — only needed if the endpoint uses a write/POST body requiring a contract mapper. A GET search does not.
8. `admin-back/lib/env/index.ts` and `deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts:177-196` — only if adding search-specific timeout/rate-limit settings. If reusing `CORE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` and `ADMIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, no deploy env change is needed.
9. No change needed in `admin-back/lib/mtlsClient/index.ts` or core mTLS middleware as long as the path remains under `/internal/admin`.

---

## 5. mTLS/config, logging, rate limits, tests, conventions

### mTLS and environment for a new endpoint

No new mTLS configuration is required for a route under the existing admin channel.

- BFF client certificate paths: `MTLS_CLIENT_CERT_PATH`, `MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_PATH`, `MTLS_CA_CERT_PATH` at `admin-back/lib/env/index.ts:18-21`.
- BFF agent uses TLS 1.3, `rejectUnauthorized: true`, keep-alive: `admin-back/lib/mtlsClient/index.ts:188-203`.
- BFF path is restricted to `/internal/admin` by `CORE_CHANNEL_PREFIX` and `assertCorePath`: `admin-back/lib/mtlsClient/index.ts:11-12`, `136-155`.
- Core `/internal/admin` is bound to `CN=admin-back`: `core-back/api/index.ts:13-16`, `core-back/api/middleware/mtlsGuard.ts:19-49`.
- Deploy cert names: `admin-back-client.crt/.key` with `CN=admin-back` at `deploy/lib/pkiManager.ts:121-125`.
- Deploy admin env: `CORE_BACK_URL`, `MTLS_*`, `ADMIN_BIND_HOST`, `ADMIN_LAN_CIDRS` at `deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts:177-196`.
- Nginx forwards `/api/` with `X-Real-IP`, `X-Request-Id`, 60s read timeout at `deploy/templates/nginx.admin.lan.conf.tpl:47-57`.

A new `/internal/admin/search` path is accepted by `assertCorePath`; a path like `/internal/search` would fail with `CORE_CHANNEL_VIOLATION`.

### Request logging

- BFF logging is global: `admin-back/index.ts:14`, implementation at `admin-back/lib/requestLogger/index.ts:103-166`.
- It includes request id, method, original URL, status, and duration.
- `resolveRequestId` accepts a safe incoming `x-request-id` or creates a UUID: `admin-back/lib/requestLogger/index.ts:38-45`.
- Header/payload redaction exists for `logger.detail` and header logging: `admin-back/lib/requestLogger/index.ts:8-36`.
- Important caveat: the log line uses `request.originalUrl` at line 135, so search terms in the query string are logged. If the search may contain PII, either use a POST body or change/redact the logged URL.
- Core logs all requests via `core-back/index.ts:65-66` and `core-back/lib/requestLogger/index.ts:165-169`.
- Core read endpoints generally do not write audit logs. Export endpoints do, e.g. recent activity export at `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:701-727`, merchants export at lines 4354-4365. A deep search over sensitive records should probably emit an audit event; that would be a new deliberate convention, not an automatic one.

### Rate limits

- All protected BFF routes share `adminLimiter` at `admin-back/api/protected/index.ts:26-39`.
  - Default max: `ADMIN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX = 600` (`admin-back/lib/env/index.ts:40`).
  - Window is hard-coded to 60 seconds at `admin-back/api/protected/index.ts:27`; `ADMIN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` exists at `admin-back/lib/env/index.ts:41` but is not used by this limiter.
- Auth routes have a separate limiter at `admin-back/api/public/auth.ts:10-23`.
- Core internal admin routes have no rate limiter. Only core’s public router has one (`core-back/api/public/index.ts:4-13`).
- A new BFF search route inherits the admin limiter. If global search is expensive, add a dedicated limiter or make the existing window configurable rather than relying solely on the shared 600/min budget.

### Tests and conventions

BFF test setup:

- `admin-back/test/helpers/core.ts:17-103` creates a test PKI with CN `admin-back`.
- `admin-back/test/helpers/core.ts:188-241` starts a fake TLS core that records every request URL, headers, and body.
- `admin-back/test/admin-surface.test.ts:43-68` defines the fetch helper; tests set env in `beforeAll`.
- Route-surface test lists every BFF route and asserts forwarding to `/internal/admin/` at `admin-back/test/admin-surface.test.ts:1129-1332`.
- Contract tests assert mappers emit only core-accepted keys and required keys against transcribed schemas: `admin-back/test/core-contract.test.ts:909-940`.
- mTLS/path/header tests: `admin-back/test/mtls-client.test.ts:16-82`.

Core tests:

- `core-back/test/internal-routes.test.ts:46-67` checks unauthenticated protected routes return `401 AUTH_REQUIRED`.
- `core-back/test/phase1-mtls-and-schema.test.ts:244-299` checks CN-to-channel binding.
- `core-back/test/list-query.test.ts` covers search, filters, dates, ranges, sorting, pagination.

For a new search endpoint, add:

- BFF route-surface test proving `/api/v1/admin/search` forwards to `/internal/admin/search` with the correct query.
- BFF test for query validation and array/CSV handling.
- Core test for unauthenticated rejection and authority-based result filtering.
- Core test for search matching, type filtering, pagination, and sensitive-field exclusion.
- If POST with a body/contract mapper, a `CORE_SCHEMAS` entry and contract test.

Conventions to preserve:

- BFF remains stateless and database-free (`admin-back/README.md:5-9`).
- Reads use `coreForward` with `querySchema`; writes use public zod schema + `bodyFrom` + core strict schema.
- Path params are validated and encoded with `encodeURIComponent`.
- Lists use `buildListQuery`/`listResponse`; do not post-filter capped arrays.
- Declare `status: 201` for creation; use `relayStatus: true` for async/core-controlled statuses.
- Use `ApiError` for stable `{ code, message, details?, reference? }` envelopes.
- Keep all new core paths under `/internal/admin`.
- Register the core route after `router.use(requireAuthentication)` at `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts:674`.
- If adding BFF `requireAuthorities`, update `ADMIN_AUTHORITY_HINTS` or the guard may silently pass.
- Prefer comma-separated filter values, not repeated query params, because BFF drops arrays.
- If search terms are sensitive, address the BFF URL logging at `admin-back/lib/requestLogger/index.ts:135`.

### Frontend UI design

Replace app bar search button with a prominent search pill (maybe existing icon stays? User wants "replace the search in app bar with deep search tool"). Current app bar has icon-only guide search. Could replace with a compact search field/pill showing "Search everything..." and shortcut `⌘K`, maybe responsive collapses to icon on mobile. Drawer guide search remains.

New component `components/search/GlobalSearchPalette.tsx`:
- VDialog maxWidth 760, top aligned.
- Use VTextField or custom input, autofocus, clear.
- Tabs/filters? Scope filter chips "All", "Records", "Pages", "Guide". Could initially show group headers. Maybe filter via typed prefixes (e.g. `merchant:acme`, `ref:...`)? Deep plan can include optional prefix syntax. But not necessary.
- Results grouped by entity type, with icons/kind badges, title, subtitle, status badge, matched reference, keyboard hints.
- Flat selection index across groups.
- Show "Pages" and "Guide" groups computed locally; "Records" from API.
- Empty state: recent searches when query empty (recents + quick links + recent records); when no results, show search tips.
- Loading skeleton/progress and error notice with retry; don't snackbar.
- Debounce 250ms, min 2 chars, request sequence guard, AbortController optional (axios supports signal).
- Cache: per-session Map normalized query -> results with TTL 30-60s; in-flight dedupe maybe.
- Recent searches localStorage key `pg-admin:global-search:recent`; store queries and optionally selected result (id/type/title/target), cap 8; clear action. Privacy: local only; maybe no PII in query? User accepted.
- Keyboard: Ctrl/Cmd+K toggles (if open, focus input); Escape close; ArrowUp/Down; Enter; Tab? `Home`/`End`; Enter on group header? Keep simple.
- Focus return to trigger on close; restore previous scroll? VDialog.
- ARIA: use `role="dialog"` with label; input `role="combobox" aria-expanded aria-controls aria-activedescendant`; listbox with groups and option ids. Vuetify VList may not expose; custom markup or add attributes. Could use `VList` with `role=listbox` and items `role=option`. Need implement.
- Mobile: full-screen-ish dialog, app bar trigger icon-only; hide shortcut label.
- i18n: add keys to catalogue for labels/hints; return raw group labels? Server returns labels? Better frontend maps type to label via i18n. Server returns type only.
- Highlight matching text? Could implement safe text split (no v-html) around normalized query, but optional. Deep plan maybe include.
- `?` help and Ctrl+K separate; Escape closes palette first if open.

parts.text:
Could design globalSearch module to accept a `PrismaLike` client or injectable client for tests. Better:
```
export const createGlobalSearchService = (db: PrismaClient) => ...
```
But admin handler can call `searchGlobal(client, ...)`; tests can pass fake client. Plan mention dependency injection.

Need fake client supports `findMany` with `where` contains? Not currently. Could either test with real DB (exhaustive harness) or extend fake. Existing fake `matches` only exact equality, no contains. Could write tests with a stub search client returning rows. Better service accepts delegate map:
```
type SearchDb = Pick<PrismaClient, "merchant"|...>
```
Test with hand stubs. Or build service with callback `searchRows(type, where, take)`.

Maybe too detailed for plan. Mention unit test ranking/authorization with stub rows; integration test with exhaustive MariaDB harness.

Need inspect exhaustive harness maybe can seed. Fine.

### UI/UX specifics and CSS

Add classes:
- `.pg-global-search-trigger` style similar `.pg-search-pill` but width 210.
- `.pg-command-dialog` maybe VCard.
- `.pg-command-input`, `.pg-command-group`, `.pg-command-item`, `.pg-command-item--active`, `.pg-command-kbd`, `.pg-command-empty`, `.pg-command-section`.
- Use CSS variables. Dark theme.
- No gradients. Shadows/radii tokens.

App bar:
Current app bar already has search icon. Replace with pill maybe. Need not overdo. "replace the search in the app bar with a deep search tool" could mean keep icon but it opens new tool. But better visual affordance: icon + "Search" + Ctrl K. We'll plan.

- Sidebar search pill stays, relabel "Search guide", remove Ctrl K hint (or show `Guide`). The user said guide search exists nav and appbar; they ask replace appbar with deep search. Keeping nav guide is per chosen answer.

### Search result grouping and interaction details
- Query with `type:` prefix? Nice but optional. Could implement simple prefix filters e.g. `merchant:acme`, `ref:TX...`, `guide:chargeback`. This is deep but adds parser. Could include in plan as phase 2? User wants deep. Maybe implement a minimal scope filter via alternating chips "All / Records / Pages / Guide" and group-specific keyboard filter. But not necessary.
Could add `type` filter chips in palette header: All, Records, Pages, Guide. Records group displays entity groups. This is useful.
- "Search everything" includes records, pages, guide. Good.

### Security details
- Server returns no fields that user cannot list currently.
- AML groups only if confidential; no counts.
- SUPPORT merchant search excludes taxId/registrationNo and result only names/status/contact? Contact might be allowed; maybe no email/phone to minimize. Search by contact email/phone could expose? Support probably can see contact. Keep.
- Search query itself can reveal a tax ID; logs: POST body not logged by default. Good.
- Response cache-control no-store.
- No `x-` raw SQL; Prisma.
- Input max 120, no wildcard injection concern.
- Rate limit and debounced client.
- Potential enumeration: Any authorized user could search all within scope; expected.

### Performance
- Per-type queries with take `limit*3`, indexes? Leading wildcard. To avoid full table scans for large tables:
  - Add `GLOBAL_SEARCH` feature flag? Maybe config `ADMIN_GLOBAL_SEARCH_TYPES`? No.
  - Limit searchable types by principal.
  - Add DB indexes for `createdAt`? Not useful.
  - Add MySQL FULLTEXT indexes? Plan optional Phase 2:
    - Add FULLTEXT indexes via Prisma migration on Merchant(legalName, tradeName, displayName), JoinRequest? (merchant relation), KybDocument(originalFileName), Gateway(name, code), etc. But FULLTEXT behavior and relevance differs. Could plan "bounded v1 with documented scale limits; if tables exceed ~X rows, add full-text or external index." The user asked plan deeply; mention.
  - Server-side in-memory cache with TTL 30s keyed by principal authority signature + query + types, LRU max 200. Could reduce load. But sensitive results caching in memory is okay? It may persist results across users; key includes principal role/authorities but not user id? Need include principal user id to avoid cross-user data leak if same authority. But results same for same authority? Some fields maybe reviewer-specific? Not. Still include user id. TTL 15s, max 100. Adds complexity. Could skip; frontend caches 60s per session. For repeated queries across operators, no cache. Hmm.
  - Existing HTTP caching none. We can plan server-side micro-cache optional. Maybe not implement initially due correctness. Keep frontend map TTL 60s.
  - Query only when query >=2 and debounce 250ms; cancel stale via sequence. Good.

- Timeout: 60s default too high; search endpoint client timeout maybe 10s via axios per request. Server query budget? Could set client timeout 10s. BFF core timeout 60s. If DB slow, user waits. Add `Promise.allSettled` per type so one failure doesn't fail whole search; return partial groups and `partial: true`. But each Prisma query could still hang. Could add a `withTimeout` per type 3s (Promise.race) but underlying query continues; could overload. Maybe no.
- `partial` field if any type errors; don't leak error details, log server-side. Good robust design.
- `tookMs`.

### Search endpoint response status
- Empty/short query: 400 validation? Frontend avoids. Better return 200 with empty groups for query <2 to simplify? Deep search endpoint should validate 2..120 and return 400 for short; but palette local uses no call. BFF z schema. Fine.
- Requested unauthorized types: ignore.
- If `types` contains unknown: 400 validation from zod enum array? Could ignore unknown or reject. Reject 400 for typos. But client might send old type; not issue. Use `z.array(z.enum(SEARCH_TYPES)).max(...)`.
- Types body is array; core strict. BFF passes. Good.
- limit 1..10 default 5. Total cap 18*5=90. Fine.

### Deep-link page details:
Need plan exact modifications and query params:
- `?open=<id>` for Approvals, AuditLog, AmlCases, AmlScreenings, AmlRules, AmlReports, Disputes, Adjustments, CashOuts, Reconciliation, Rails, GatewayRoutes.
- `?search=<term>` for GatewayInquirySchedules fallback.
- `?tab=transactions&reference=<ref>` on MerchantDetail.
- `?entry=<id>` guide existing.
- Maybe `?open=<id>` on AdminUsers? already detail route.
- For gateway -> `GatewayWizard` route.
- For inquiries with operatorCaseId -> detail route; else search fallback.
- For audit log exact open -> new detail API.
- For rails/routes, fetch detail by id before open; add skeleton loading.
- On query open, ensure not reopen repeatedly with a `handledDeepLink` Set or clear query after successful open. Plan clear query via `router.replace({ query: {...route.query, open: undefined} })`? Vue Router removes undefined? Use destructure. Clearing after open is cleaner and prevents refresh reopen? But deep link requires refresh reopen; if cleared immediately, user can't share URL after open. For a palette navigation, the URL should remain shareable; but closing modal leaves URL. Not harmful. Could keep and use Set to only handle once per id. On page refresh, reopens (desired). On modal close, doesn't reopen because no query change. Implement `lastHandled` ref. Good.

- Search result click should close palette before navigating and maybe clear local query? Clear query? Recents stored. Keep last query? Maybe reset after navigation. Plan: close, push, reset query on next open? Could keep to show recent. The user may open again. Better reset query after selection but keep recents. Good.

### Tests for open deep links
E2E with real API maybe not easy but can use routes. Plan add targeted tests.

### Documentation
- Update `design/ui/portal_ui_implementation_plan.md` and maybe new `design/ui/admin_global_search.md`.
- Update admin-back README route list.
- Update `docs`? no.

### Implementation order
Need present plan with phases. Since user says "plan it very deeply and lets implement it" but plan mode now. We must not implement. Final should be plan, maybe mention awaiting approval to implement. We should be comprehensive but concise enough. Desired oververbosity 5, but user asked deep plan. We can produce substantial plan.

Need perhaps include "out of scope" / decisions:
- No external search engine (Elasticsearch/Meilisearch) in v1.
- No server-side search history/telemetry.
- No cross-app merchant/checkout portals; admin only.
- No changes to money/auth invariants.
- No full-text index migration initially? Maybe mention optional after volume.
- Guide nav remains.

Need maybe include "open exact record" means modifying many pages; list all files and exact query params. Good.

Potential issue: `admin-front` UI compliance gate forbids raw VDialog/VChip/VCard in route pages. New component under components is fine. Use `VCard` there. Fine.

Potential issue: `FormModal` only sizes up to 760; command palette needs 760-820. Could use raw VDialog as existing guide modal. Component under components allowed. Use `VDialog maxWidth=760/820`.

Potential issue: app bar search trigger width; CSS responsive.

Potential issue: Search guide modal state still in layout. Ctrl+K now global. Guide page mounts modal; no conflict.

Potential issue: `onGlobalKeydown` Escape closes both; global first. Also when palette input focused and user types `?`, typing guard prevents help drawer. Good.
- Ctrl+K should toggle; if dialog open, focus input; maybe close? Usually toggles focus. Plan: if closed open; if open focus input, not close. Or Ctrl+K toggles close. Choose open/focus.
- `/` shortcut? optional. Could add `/` to open when not typing. Nice but not necessary. Add? Deep search UX usually `/` or Cmd+K. We can include `/` as optional. But `?` already help. `/` unused. Good.

Potential issue: `$` commands? no.

Potential issue: recent searches storing sensitive terms in localStorage. User accepted local recents. Add note: only store queries and selected item labels; never server. Provide clear all. If AML/confidential searches stored locally on shared workstation, risk. Could choose to store only query, not result metadata; but user chose local recents. Use localStorage with clear action. Maybe store max 8 with 7-day expiry, and exclude records marked confidential? All AML result labels could be sensitive. Better metadata includes type/title, and if type starts aml, store only query? Hmm. Security. Deep plan can say:
  - Recents store query text plus minimal target (type/id/title). Because admin workstation shared, add "Clear recent searches" and do not store full subtitles. Could avoid storing AML result titles? But query itself may contain AML subject. Local storage is per browser, same as session. Accept.
  - Maybe store only query strings, not result metadata. Clicking recent re-runs search, so no record titles stored. That's safer and simpler. Yes: recent searches = last 8 query strings, no result data. On click, set query and re-run. This satisfies "local recents" and avoids storing IDs. Plan mention. Good.

Potential issue: server logs via `requestLogger.detail`? POST body isn't logged. Good.

Potential issue: CORS? Admin front same origin via API. Fine.

Potential issue: `urlsMap` path excludes `/api`; baseURL adds. Good.

Potential issue: Add `auditLogDetail` and maybe `gatewayInquiryDetail` exists already. Fine.

Potential issue: Need add `attemptDetail`? For transaction deep link we may not need; use reference. Search result includes merchantId+reference. Good.

Potential issue: Search result deep link to merchant detail with reference requires merchant transactions API search by reference and `attempt:read`? The transaction endpoint requires `merchant:read`. Search attempt group should require `attempt:read` AND `merchant:read`? If user has attempt:read but not merchant:read, target page unauthorized. Core seed OPERATOR has attempt:read/case:read but maybe no merchant:read; operator can open merchant detail? route authority requires merchants.read or support.read_merchant. So target might fail. To avoid, require both `attempt:read` and one of `merchant:read` for payment_attempt search results. Or target OperatorCases? Attempt may not have case. Better require `merchant:read` OR `support.read_merchant` (core merchant:read) plus attempt:read. Use `hasAny(["merchant:read"]) && hasAny(["attempt:read"])`. But support has merchant:read and attempt:read per seed. If operator lacks merchant:read, omit attempts. Alternatively target merchant detail maybe route accessible for operator? routesAuthorities says merchants.read or support.read_merchant, so no. Good.

  2. **Records** — permission-filtered server results.
  3. **Guide** — local `searchGuide()` results.
- Empty query shows recent query strings and quick page links.
- Selecting a result closes the palette, stores the query locally, and opens the exact record or a valid fallback.
- Recent searches are stored locally as query strings only, capped at 8, with a clear action. No record IDs or result payloads are stored.

### 2. API contract

Use a dedicated `POST` endpoint because search terms may contain PII; `admin-back` logs `originalUrl`, and POST keeps terms out of URL logs.

```text
POST /api/v1/admin/search
-> POST /internal/admin/search
```

Request:

```ts
{
  query: string;        // trimmed, 2..120 chars
  types?: SearchType[]; // optional allow-list
  limit?: number;       // per-group cap, 1..10, default 5
}
```

Response:

```ts
{
  query: string;
  groups: Array<{
    type: SearchType;
    items: Array<{
      id: string;
      title: string;
      subtitle?: string;
      reference?: string;
      status?: string;
      merchantId?: string;
      operatorCaseId?: string;
    }>;
    truncated: boolean;
  }>;
  total: number;
  tookMs: number;
  partial: boolean;
}
```

Add `Cache-Control: no-store`. Do not return route names from the server; the frontend maps `type + id` to routes.

### 3. Server-side search groups

New module: `core-back/lib/globalSearch.ts`, injected with the Prisma client so it is testable.

| Group | Core authority | Primary match fields | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| `merchant` | `merchant:read` | id, legal/trade/display name, contact email/phone; tax/reg only with sensitive access | Merchant detail |
| `payment_attempt` | `attempt:read` + `merchant:read` | id, reference, provider/network/gateway refs | Merchant detail transactions |
| `join_request` | `kyb:read` or `compliance:read` | id, merchant names/contact | Join request detail |
| `kyb_document` | `kyb:read` or `compliance:read` | id, file name, SHA-256, merchant names | KYB document detail |
| `user` | `user:read` or `security:read` | id, email, phone | Admin user detail |
| `approval` | `approval:read` | id, subject id/type, maker/checker email | Approvals `?open=` |
| `audit_log` | `security:read` | id, action, entity type/id, actor email | Audit log `?open=` |
| `aml_case` | confidential AML access | id, subject id, trigger reason, rule code/name/reviewer email | AML cases `?open=` |
| `aml_screening` | confidential AML access | id, subject id, provider code/request ref | AML screenings `?open=` |
| `aml_rule` | confidential AML access | id, code, name | AML rules `?open=` |
| `aml_report` | confidential AML access | id, report ref, subject id, submission ref | AML reports `?open=` |
| `operator_case` | `case:read` or `operator:read` | id, attempt refs, merchant names, recon refs | Operator case detail |
| `gateway_inquiry` | `case:read` or `operator:read` | id, attempt refs, merchant names | Linked operator case, else inquiry list with `?search=` |
| `dispute` | `dispute:read` | id, external dispute ref, reason code, attempt ref, merchant trade name | Disputes `?open=` |
| `adjustment` | `finance:read` | id, reason, dispute/provider refs, source attempt ref | Adjustments `?open=` |
| `cashout` | `cashout:read` | id, wallet id, merchant trade name | Cash-outs `?open=` |
| `reconciliation_run` | `reconciliation:read` | id, file name, gateway code/name | Reconciliation `?open=` |
| `gateway` | `gateway:read` | id, code, name, operator | Gateway wizard |
| `rail` | `gateway:read` | id, code, English/Arabic name | Rails `?open=` |
| `route` | `gateway:read` | id, rail code, gateway code | Routes `?open=` |

Explicitly deferred because there is no exact-record destination in the current UI: commission profiles, velocity rules, credential sets, platform settings.

### 4. Server implementation details

- Extract the AML confidential predicate into a shared helper so `admin.ts` and search cannot drift.
- Filter groups by authority **before** querying. Unauthorized groups must not appear in `groups`, `total`, or counts.
- Per type, fetch `limit * 3` rows, rank in memory, then slice:
  - exact ID/reference/code/title/email/phone: highest;
  - prefix match: next;
  - substring match: next;
  - then newest first.
- Use Prisma `select` only; never select ciphertext, secrets, payout accounts, AML match-list names, or audit `beforeJson`/`afterJson`.
- Execute group queries with `Promise.allSettled`; return `partial: true` if one group fails, and log the failure server-side with request ID.
- Validate the body independently in core even though the BFF validates it.
- Add a search-specific limit of roughly 120 requests/minute keyed by a hash of the session token, in addition to the existing admin limiter.
- Add `GET /internal/admin/audit-logs/:id` plus BFF proxy `GET /api/v1/admin/audit-logs/:id` because audit logs currently have no detail endpoint. Register `/:id` after static routes such as `/export`.

- New: `core-back/lib/globalSearch.ts`
- Modify: `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts` after `requireAuthentication` at line 674
- Modify: `core-back/lib/auth/...` or a small shared access helper
- New: `admin-back/api/protected/search.ts`
- Modify: `admin-back/api/protected/index.ts` to mount `/search` before root routers
- Modify: `admin-back/api/protected/auditLogs.ts`
- Modify: `admin-front/src/constants/urlsMap/index.ts`
- Tests: new core search tests, BFF surface tests, audit-detail tests

### 5. Frontend palette

New folder: `admin-front/src/components/search/`

- `types.ts` — search types, group/item/response types.
- `api.ts` — `api.post(urlsMap.globalSearch, body, { timeout: 8000 })`, sequence guard and abort support.
- `targets.ts` — maps result type to route/deep-link target.
- `recents.ts` — localStorage query history, capped at 8.
- `GlobalSearchPalette.tsx` — the command palette UI.
- `SearchResultRow.tsx` — optional shared result row.
- `localCommands.ts` — pages from `useSections()` and guide results from `searchGuide()`.

UX details:
- `VDialog` max width ~780px, top aligned, scrollable; component lives under `components/` so it does not violate the UI abstraction gate.
- Input: autofocus, clear button, search icon, `Ctrl K` hint.
- Filter chips: `All`, `Records`, `Pages`, `Guide`.
- Group headers with result counts; active row highlighted; ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End/Enter/Escape.
- Loading progress; local error state with retry, no snackbar spam.
- Empty state distinguishes “no query” (recents/quick links) from “no results.”
- Result rows show icon, title, subtitle, optional status badge, and kind.
- Debounce 250ms; require 2 characters before server search.
- Cache results per session for 60s keyed by query + limit + types.
- Safe text highlighting only; no `v-html`.
- ARIA combobox/listbox, `aria-activedescendant`, result-count live region, focus trap, focus returned to trigger.
- Responsive and RTL/dark-mode safe using existing tokens and logical CSS.
- CSS classes: `.pg-global-search-trigger`, `.pg-command-dialog`, `.pg-command-item`, `.pg-command-item--active`, `.pg-command-kbd`, `.pg-command-empty`, `.pg-command-group`.

Layout integration in `admin-front/src/layouts/default.tsx`:
- Replace app-bar search button at lines 226-233 with the global trigger.
- Keep `GlobalGuideSearchModal` and the drawer pill for guide-only search.
- Change `Ctrl/Cmd+K` at lines 135-141 to open global search.
- Ensure Escape closes the topmost overlay and focus returns correctly.
- Keep `?` help shortcut behavior.

### 6. Exact-record deep links

Add a small shared `useOpenQuery` helper and one-shot handling so the same query does not reopen a drawer repeatedly.

| Page | Query support |
|---|---|
| Approvals | `?open=<id>` → fetch detail and open drawer |
| Audit Log | `?open=<id>` → new detail endpoint, open drawer |
| AML cases/screenings/rules/reports | `?open=<id>` → fetch detail, open drawer |
| Disputes | `?open=<id>` → fetch detail, open drawer |
| Adjustments | `?open=<id>` → fetch detail, open drawer |
| Cash-outs | `?open=<id>` → fetch detail, open drawer |
| Reconciliation | `?open=<id>` → fetch run detail, open drawer |
| Rails | `?open=<id>` → fetch rail detail, open dialog |
| Routes | `?open=<id>` → fetch route detail, open edit dialog |
| Gateway inquiries | linked case route, otherwise `?search=<term>` prefill |
| Merchant detail | `?tab=transactions&reference=<ref>` → open transactions tab, prefill search, open matching attempt drawer |
| Guide | existing `?entry=<id>` |

For merchant attempts:
- Add `initialSearch` and `focusReference` support to `MerchantResourceTable`.
- On rows loaded, find the exact reference, open `MerchantTransactionDialog` once, and keep the URL shareable.
- Server search returns `merchantId` + `reference` for attempt results.

Frontend additionally filters results through `routesAuthorities`, `routesRoles`, and section visibility so a user never sees a result that leads to a route the UI hides.

### 7. Performance and security guards

- No database migration in v1; reuse existing tables and list-query conventions.
- Bound all queries; no pagination in the palette.
- Return only minimal safe metadata, never full records.
- No hidden AML/finance counts or “no results” hints.
- SUPPORT merchant search excludes tax/registration fields and result payloads never expose sensitive fields.
- Search terms are not written to server logs because the endpoint uses a POST body.
- Add slow-search logging (`tookMs`) and a future path: if audit/reconciliation tables grow, add MySQL FULLTEXT indexes or an external index rather than escalating wildcard queries.
- No new runtime dependency.

### 8. Tests and verification

Backend:
- Core search service: validation, ranking, truncation, group ordering, partial failure.
- Authority matrix: SUPPORT, OPERATOR, FINANCE, COMPLIANCE/MLRO, GATEWAY_ADMIN, SECURITY_ADMIN.
- Redaction: no AML groups for unauthorized users, no sensitive merchant fields, no audit JSON.
- Route tests: 401 unauthenticated, 400 invalid body, `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- BFF tests: `/search` forwarding, body validation, audit-detail proxy, rate limiting, error relay.
- Extend `admin-back/test/admin-surface.test.ts` route surface.

Frontend:
- Unit tests for target mapping, recents, local command index, Arabic/RTL labels, and result normalization.
- E2E new `tests/e2e/admin/global-search.spec.ts`:
  - app-bar trigger and drawer guide trigger remain separate;
  - Ctrl+K opens/focuses palette;
  - debounce/mocked API displays grouped results;
  - keyboard navigation and Enter navigation;
  - Escape/focus return;
  - `?open=` deep links open drawers;
  - unauthorized groups absent;
  - mobile, RTL, dark mode, and a11y;
  - malicious result text rendered as text.
- Extend `shell.spec.ts` and `a11y.spec.ts`.

Final gates:
- `core-back`: typecheck, targeted tests, full test suite.
- `admin-back`: typecheck, tests.
- `admin-front`: typecheck, unit tests, build.
- Playwright global-search, shell, a11y, geometry.
- Live verification with real data and at least two authority profiles.
- Deploy core + admin edge/frontend; verify health and deep links.

### 9. Implementation order

1. Add API contract/design note and `core-back/lib/globalSearch.ts`.
2. Add core `POST /search` and audit-log detail endpoint.
3. Add BFF `search.ts`, audit-detail proxy, URL map entries.
4. Build `GlobalSearchPalette`, local commands/guide integration, recents, CSS, i18n.
5. Replace app-bar trigger and wire Ctrl+K.
6. Add exact-record deep links to all affected pages.
7. Add tests and fix security/performance edge cases.
8. Run full gates, deploy, and verify live.

No files have been changed yet. Approve this plan and I’ll implement it in this order.

 # admin-back
 
 LAN-only admin edge API for the payment gateway platform.
 
 - Runtime: Bun + Express 5 + Zod 4.
 - No database access: no Prisma client, no `DATABASE_*` variable, no migration script.
 - Every operation is forwarded over mutual TLS to `core-back` through `lib/mtlsClient/index.ts` using the client certificate identified by `CN=admin-back`.
 - The server binds to `ADMIN_BIND_HOST` (default `127.0.0.1`) and every `/api/v1/admin/*` call is restricted to `ADMIN_LAN_CIDRS`.
 - Role and authority hints are read from the bearer token for coarse grained gating only; `core-back` remains the authoritative authority, re-verifying the signature, revocation, MFA state, IP allowlist and the `authorities_map` on every call.
 
 ## Routes
 
 Mounted under `/api/v1/admin`:
 
 | Area | Routes |
 | :--- | :--- |
 | Auth | `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/mfa` |
+| Deep search | `POST /search` (token-hashed 120 req/min limiter; forwards to core) |

+const compact = (values: Array<string | null | undefined>): string =>
+  values.filter((value): value is string => Boolean(value)).join(" · ");
+
+const amountText = (value: unknown): string => {
+  const numeric = Number(value ?? 0);

+const asRecord = (value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> =>
+  value !== null && typeof value === "object" && !Array.isArray(value)
+    ? (value as Record<string, unknown>)
+    : {};

+const scopedStatusIn = <T extends string>(
+  parsed: ParsedSearchQuery,
+  allowed: Record<string, string>,
+): T | undefined => {
+  if (!parsed.scopedStatus) {
+    return undefined;
+  }
+  return Object.values(allowed).includes(parsed.scopedStatus)
+    ? (parsed.scopedStatus as T)
+    : undefined;
+};

+type ErasedSearchProvider = SearchProviderPlugin<unknown>;
+
+export class SearchProviderRegistry {
+  private readonly providers = new Map<string, ErasedSearchProvider>();
+
+  public register<TRow>(plugin: SearchProviderPlugin<TRow>): this {
+    this.providers.set(plugin.type, {
+      type: plugin.type,
+      aliases: plugin.aliases,
+      order: plugin.order,
+      canAccess: plugin.canAccess,
+      supportsTokenKind: plugin.supportsTokenKind,
+      fetchCandidates: (context) => plugin.fetchCandidates(context),
+      extractMatchSignals: (row, actor) =>
+        plugin.extractMatchSignals(row as TRow, actor),
+      toResultItem: (row, actor) => plugin.toResultItem(row as TRow, actor),
+    });
+    return this;
+  }
+
+  public unregister(type: SearchType): boolean {
+    return this.providers.delete(type);
+  }
+
+  public get(type: SearchType): ErasedSearchProvider | undefined {
+    return this.providers.get(type);
+  }
+
+  public getAllOrdered(): ErasedSearchProvider[] {
+    return Array.from(this.providers.values()).sort((a, b) => {
+      if (a.order !== b.order) {
+        return a.order - b.order;
+      }
+      return a.type.localeCompare(b.type);
+    });
+  }
+
+  public getRegisteredTypes(): Set<string> {
+    return new Set(this.providers.keys());
+  }
+
+  public resolveAliasToTypes(alias: string): SearchType[] {
+    const normalized = alias.toLowerCase().trim();
+    const matches: SearchType[] = [];
+    for (const plugin of this.providers.values()) {
+      if (
+        plugin.type.toLowerCase() === normalized ||
+        plugin.aliases?.some(
+          (candidate) => candidate.toLowerCase() === normalized,
+        )
+      ) {
+        matches.push(plugin.type);
+      }
+    }
+    return matches;
+  }
+}

+  registry.register(plugin);

+};

+export const globalSearchRequestSchema = z
+  .object({
+    query: z
+      .string()
+      .transform((value) => value.trim())
+      .pipe(
+        z
+          .string()
+          .min(2, "Query must be at least 2 characters")
+          .max(120, "Query must be at most 120 characters"),
+      ),
+    types: z.array(z.string().min(1).max(64)).optional(),
+    limit: z.number().int().min(1).max(10).default(5),
+  })
+  .strict();

+export interface GlobalSearchLogger {
+  warn: (message: string, meta?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
+  error: (message: string, meta?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
+}
+
+export interface ExecuteGlobalSearchDeps {
+  prisma: PrismaClient;
+  actor: AuthenticatedAdminActor;
+  requestId?: string;
+  logger?: GlobalSearchLogger;
+  registry?: SearchProviderRegistry;
+}
+
+export async function executeGlobalSearch(
+  rawBody: unknown,
+  deps: ExecuteGlobalSearchDeps,
+): Promise<GlobalSearchResponse> {
+  const startedAt = performance.now();
+  const registry = deps.registry ?? defaultSearchRegistry;
+  const validated = parseOrThrow(globalSearchRequestSchema, rawBody);
+  const registeredTypes = registry.getRegisteredTypes();
+  const requestedTypes = validated.types;
+
+  if (requestedTypes) {
+    const invalid = requestedTypes.filter(
+      (type) => !registeredTypes.has(type),
+    );
+    if (invalid.length > 0) {
+      throw new ApiError(
+        400,
+        "SEARCH_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED",
+        "The search request contains an unsupported record type",
+        { types: invalid },
+      );
+    }
+  }
+
+  const parsed = parseSearchQuery(validated.query);
+  const limit = validated.limit;
+  const take = limit * 3;
+
+  let allowedTypeSet: Set<string> | null = requestedTypes
+    ? new Set(requestedTypes)
+    : null;
+
+  if (parsed.scopedTypeAliases.length > 0) {
+    const aliasMatched = new Set<string>();
+    for (const alias of parsed.scopedTypeAliases) {
+      for (const matchedType of registry.resolveAliasToTypes(alias)) {
+        aliasMatched.add(matchedType);
+      }
+    }
+    if (aliasMatched.size > 0) {
+      allowedTypeSet = allowedTypeSet
+        ? new Set(
+            [...allowedTypeSet].filter((type) => aliasMatched.has(type)),
+          )
+        : aliasMatched;
+    }
+  }
+
+  const authorizedProviders = registry.getAllOrdered().filter((plugin) => {
+    if (allowedTypeSet && !allowedTypeSet.has(plugin.type)) {
+      return false;
+    }
+    if (!plugin.canAccess(deps.actor)) {
+      return false;
+    }
+    if (
+      plugin.supportsTokenKind &&
+      !plugin.supportsTokenKind(parsed)
+    ) {
+      return false;
+    }
+    return true;
+  });
+
+  const settledResults = await Promise.allSettled(
+    authorizedProviders.map(async (plugin) => {
+      const rows = await plugin.fetchCandidates({
+        prisma: deps.prisma,
+        parsed,
+        actor: deps.actor,
+        take,
+      });
+      const ranked = rankAndSliceCandidates(
+        rows,
+        plugin,
+        parsed,
+        deps.actor,
+        limit,
+      );
+      return {
+        type: plugin.type,
+        items: ranked.items,
+        truncated: ranked.truncated,
+      } satisfies SearchResultGroup;
+    }),
+  );
+
+  const groups: SearchResultGroup[] = [];
+  let total = 0;
+  let partial = false;
+
+  settledResults.forEach((result, index) => {
+    const plugin = authorizedProviders[index];
+    if (!plugin) {
+      return;
+    }
+    if (result.status === "fulfilled") {
+      if (result.value.items.length > 0) {
+        groups.push(result.value);
+        total += result.value.items.length;
+      }
+      return;
+    }
+
+    partial = true;
+    deps.logger?.error("Global search provider failed", {
+      requestId: deps.requestId,
+      providerType: plugin.type,
+      actorId: deps.actor.id,
+      error:
+        result.reason instanceof Error
+          ? result.reason.message
+          : String(result.reason),
+    });
+  });
+
+  const tookMs = Math.max(1, Math.round(performance.now() - startedAt));
+  if (tookMs > 750) {
+    deps.logger?.warn("Slow global search execution detected", {
+      requestId: deps.requestId,
+      tookMs,
+      providerCount: authorizedProviders.length,
+      totalReturned: total,
+      partial,
+    });
+  }
+
+  return {
+    query: validated.query,
+    groups,
+    total,
+    tookMs,
+    partial,
+  };
+}

model OperatorCase {
  id                   String               @id @default(uuid(7))
  createdAt            DateTime             @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt            DateTime             @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  attemptId            String?              @map("attempt_id")
  reconciliationItemId String?              @unique @map("reconciliation_item_id")
  kind                 OperatorCaseKind
  priority             OperatorCasePriority
  slaDueAt             DateTime             @map("sla_due_at")
  state                OperatorCaseState    @default(OPEN)
  assigneeUserId       String?              @map("assignee_user_id")
  resolutionNotes      String?              @map("resolution_notes") @db.Text
  approvalRequestId    String?              @map("approval_request_id")

  attempt            PaymentAttempt?          @relation(fields: [attemptId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  reconciliationItem ReconciliationItem?      @relation("OperatorCaseReconciliationItem", fields: [reconciliationItemId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  assignee           User?                    @relation("OperatorCaseAssignee", fields: [assigneeUserId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  approvalRequest    ApprovalRequest?         @relation("OperatorCaseApproval", fields: [approvalRequestId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  inquirySchedules   GatewayInquirySchedule[]

  @@index([state, priority])
  @@index([state, createdAt])
  @@index([priority])
  @@index([kind])
  @@index([slaDueAt])
  @@index([assigneeUserId])
  @@index([attemptId])
  @@map("operator_cases")
}

/// A persisted gateway status-inquiry schedule.
///
/// `payment_attempts.next_check_at` remains the durable timer that the poll
/// worker uses; this row records why the inquiry was requested, who requested
/// it, the latest status and the action history for the operator portal.
model GatewayInquirySchedule {
  id                  String                       @id @default(uuid(7))
  createdAt           DateTime                     @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt           DateTime                     @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  attemptId           String                       @map("attempt_id")
  operatorCaseId      String?                      @map("operator_case_id")
  source              GatewayInquiryScheduleSource @default(OPERATOR_CASE)
  status              GatewayInquiryScheduleStatus @default(SCHEDULED)
  scheduledByUserId   String?                      @map("scheduled_by_user_id")
  reason              String?                      @db.Text
  checklist           Json?
  previousNextCheckAt DateTime?                    @map("previous_next_check_at")
  windowStartedAt     DateTime?                    @map("window_started_at")
  nextRunAt           DateTime                     @map("next_run_at")
  lastRunAt           DateTime?                    @map("last_run_at")
  attempts            Int                          @default(0)
  lastResult          String?                      @map("last_result") @db.Text
  lastError           String?                      @map("last_error") @db.Text
  completedAt         DateTime?                    @map("completed_at")
  cancelledAt         DateTime?                    @map("cancelled_at")
  cancelledByUserId   String?                      @map("cancelled_by_user_id")
  cancelReason        String?                      @map("cancel_reason") @db.Text

  attempt      PaymentAttempt @relation(fields: [attemptId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  operatorCase OperatorCase?  @relation(fields: [operatorCaseId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  scheduledBy  User?          @relation("GatewayInquiryScheduledBy", fields: [scheduledByUserId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  cancelledBy  User?          @relation("GatewayInquiryCancelledBy", fields: [cancelledByUserId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@index([status, nextRunAt])
  @@index([attemptId, status])
  @@index([operatorCaseId])
  @@index([source, status])
  @@map("gateway_inquiry_schedules")
}

model ReconciliationRun {
  id                String    @id @default(uuid(7))
  createdAt         DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt         DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  statementSourceId String    @map("statement_source_id")
  windowStart       DateTime  @map("window_start")
  windowEnd         DateTime  @map("window_end")
  fileHash          String    @unique @map("file_hash") @db.Char(64)
  statsJson         Json      @map("stats_json")
  /// The name of the uploaded statement file.
  fileName          String?   @map("file_name") @db.Text
  /// The uploaded statement file itself: the reconciliation is a background
  /// job, so the bytes have to survive the request that stored them.
  fileContent       Bytes?    @map("file_content") @db.LongBlob
  /// Set when the background reconciliation job finished the run. It is the
  /// idempotency marker of the ingestion: a retried job never matches the
  /// same statement twice.
  ingestedAt        DateTime? @map("ingested_at")

  statementSource StatementSource      @relation(fields: [statementSourceId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  items           ReconciliationItem[]

  @@index([statementSourceId])
  @@index([ingestedAt])
model Adjustment {
  id                 String          @id @default(uuid(7))
  createdAt          DateTime        @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt          DateTime        @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  type               AdjustmentType

/// A persisted gateway status-inquiry schedule.
///
/// `payment_attempts.next_check_at` remains the durable timer that the poll
/// worker uses; this row records why the inquiry was requested, who requested
/// it, the latest status and the action history for the operator portal.
model GatewayInquirySchedule {
  id                  String                       @id @default(uuid(7))
  createdAt           DateTime                     @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt           DateTime                     @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  attemptId           String                       @map("attempt_id")

  status              GatewayInquiryScheduleStatus @default(SCHEDULED)

  reason              String?                      @db.Text
  checklist           Json?
  previousNextCheckAt DateTime?                    @map("previous_next_check_at")
  windowStartedAt     DateTime?                    @map("window_started_at")
  nextRunAt           DateTime                     @map("next_run_at")
  lastRunAt           DateTime?                    @map("last_run_at")
  attempts            Int                          @default(0)
  lastResult          String?                      @map("last_result") @db.Text
  lastError           String?                      @map("last_error") @db.Text
  completedAt         DateTime?                    @map("completed_at")
  cancelledAt         DateTime?                    @map("cancelled_at")
  cancelledByUserId   String?                      @map("cancelled_by_user_id")
  cancelReason        String?                      @map("cancel_reason") @db.Text

  attempt      PaymentAttempt @relation(fields: [attemptId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  operatorCase OperatorCase?  @relation(fields: [operatorCaseId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  scheduledBy  User?          @relation("GatewayInquiryScheduledBy", fields: [scheduledByUserId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@index([source, status])
  @@map("gateway_inquiry_schedules")
}

/// The durable job queue of `core-back`.
///
/// The queue is drained by the stateless `BackgroundJobWorker`, which claims
/// the due jobs with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. `available_at` is
/// the durable timer of the retry backoff and `locked_at` is the lease of the
/// node that currently owns the job.
model BackgroundJob {
  id            String             @id @default(uuid(7))
  createdAt     DateTime           @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt     DateTime           @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  jobType       BackgroundJobType  @map("job_type")
  referenceType String             @map("reference_type")
  referenceId   String             @map("reference_id")
  payloadJson   Json               @map("payload_json")
  state         BackgroundJobState @default(QUEUED)
  attempts      Int                @default(0)
  maxAttempts   Int                @default(5) @map("max_attempts")
  availableAt   DateTime           @default(now()) @map("available_at")
  lockedAt      DateTime?          @map("locked_at")
  lastError     String?            @map("last_error") @db.Text
  completedAt   DateTime?          @map("completed_at")

  @@index([state, availableAt])
  @@index([state, lockedAt])
  @@index([referenceType, referenceId])
  @@map("background_jobs")
}

   - ApprovalRequest: `subjectType`, `subjectId`, `state`, `mode`, `maker`, `checker`; no actionType/status/makerEmail columns

   - Dispute: `externalDisputeRef`, `reasonCode`, `amount`, `currency`, `status`, `attempt` relation with reference+merchant; no attemptReference/merchant columns
   - Adjustment: `type`, `amount`, `reason`, `externalDisputeRef`, `providerRefundRef`, `state`, `sourceAttempt` relation; no adjustmentReference/status/merchantId
   - CashoutRequest model: `amount`, `walletId`, `state`, `merchant` relation; no cashoutReference/bank ref/merchantId column except FK

   - RailRoute: `rail`/`gateway` relations, `priority`, `status`, `healthState`
   - User: `email`, `phone`, `role`, `status`, no fullName
   - AuditLog: `actor` relation for email; `action`, `entityType`, `entityId`; no actorEmail/requestId columns

6. Orchestrator `executeGlobalSearch`:

   - reject unknown registered types with a 400-compatible error; use existing `ApiError` from `../../lib/error` so core error envelope stays consistent.

Ctrl+K isn't opening palette in test. Snapshot shows no dialog. Why? Maybe `Control+k` in Playwright with lowercase? The layout listener on window keydown. It should. But `event.key` in Playwright is "k"; ctrl true. Maybe because page's browser intercepts Ctrl+K? In headless Chromium, Ctrl+K focuses omnibox? Playwright keyboard may not. Could use `page.keyboard.press("Control+KeyK")`? Standard "Control+k". Hmm.

Maybe app bar trigger opens, but Ctrl+K handler registered before? `onMounted` window listener. Should. The first test clicked trigger and opened palette, then Escape closed. So trigger works. In second test `page.goto("/dashboard")` and immediately `keyboard.press`. Maybe page not fully mounted? It waits for load, but onMounted may not registered? `page.goto` waits load; app mounts after; `page.keyboard.press` immediately maybe before Vue mounts? Snapshot shows app rendered, but perhaps keypress occurred before listener registered. Need wait for trigger visible before pressing. Test should wait. Could also make shortcut via `page.keyboard.press` after `expect(trigger).toBeVisible()`. Add wait. That likely fixes.
- First test strict label fix use getByRole textbox name regex.
- Audit deep link not opening: need inspect screenshot/error context. Could be because mockApi override order wrong or `useOpenQuery` not running due `route.query.open` initial watcher before page? It should. But maybe `AuditLog` page calls `api.get(urlsMap.auditLogDetail(id))`; `urlsMap.auditLogDetail` is `v1/admin/audit-logs/id`. `mockApi` matches path ending `/audit-logs/audit-1`; override should return. But second `mockApi` call registers after first. It should. Maybe page route guard? Admin session has `security:read`? ALL_ADMIN_UI_AUTHORITIES includes? It does not include `security:read`! Audit Log route authority requires security:read; seeded admin lacks it, so route redirect to Dashboard. Snapshot likely dashboard. Need add security:read to fixture or custom session. Existing adminSession all authorities doesn't include security:read, case:read, operator:read, dispute:read. For test audit, create custom session with security:read. Could add to ALL_ADMIN_UI_AUTHORITIES? That changes other tests maybe but more representative. Better in test seed custom session with `authoritiesMap` spread plus security:read. Do that.
- The search result merchant group works with admin session (merchants.read).
- First test guide label strict. fix.

Let's patch tests.

const scopedStatusIn = <T extends string>(parsed, values: Record<string,string>): T|undefined => {

}
